findings.title: Derived comparison overflow can prevent the final failure receipt from being written
findings.evidence: metric verifies finite inputs, but does not verify error=(a-b).abs() or scaled before converting their maxima to Python floats. Finite float32 operands can overflow subtraction. The nonfinite diagnostic is then stored in case/value or private comparison records. Profile.save uses json.dumps(..., allow_nan=False). The same contaminated case remains in receipt after the exception, and the final write also uses allow_nan=False.
findings.consequence: The run stops, but the final FAILED receipt may not be published; the last successfully saved local receipt can remain RUNNING or ENTERING. The advertised ordinary failure-receipt guarantee does not cover this branch. External exit custody could detect the exception, but does not make the internal receipt writer reliable.
findings.required_remedy: Reject nonfinite derived error/scaled tensors before storing any metric row, or serialize the failure diagnostics in a finite/JSON-safe representation without accepting the comparison. Preserve the original thresholds, then seal and independently review a successor source packet.

nonblocking_root_custody_requirements.description: admission verifies an external REVIEW.json descriptor and root adoption booleans, but does not parse that review to require this manifest, an accepting disposition, or freshness. Root must bind and adopt the actual fresh review of this exact packet; descriptor verification alone cannot enforce that semantic relation.

Admission and output creation occur before the receipt try/finally. Root external elapsed/exit custody must cover those failures and native termination; the packet expressly assigns startup/admission to root external custody.

The fixed positive minimum free-device bytes is an admission precondition rather than a proved memory ceiling. Multiple CPU token banks, retained mixed graphs, materialized arrays and diagnostic temporaries coexist. Current availability and external custody remain root responsibilities.
Runtime admission binds declared files/settings/version/device UUID, not a complete linked or transitive runtime closure; this review read metadata only, and did not revalidate the remote runtime.
